title: Yarrow bath for aching legs
subtitle: A full-body or foot bath of Achillea millefolium for muscular aching and tired legs
excerpt: Yarrow bath is a strong decoction of dried yarrow herb added to a warm bath or foot bath for tired, aching legs and general muscular soreness. Yarrow is a circulatory herb, the diaphoretic and tonic actions work with the warmth of the bath to ease congestion in the legs and bring surface circulation to the skin. 100 g of dried herb per full bath; 25 g per foot bath. A 20-minute soak.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), yarrow entry, Botanical.com. Nicholas Culpeper, Complete Herbal (1653), yarrow entry, public domain.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Decoct the yarrow fresh each time. Do not store the strained liquid.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb that promotes perspiration and opens the capillaries near the skin surface, traditionally used to support the body's temperature regulation and to move stagnant circulation to the periphery. Yarrow is considered a cooling diaphoretic.

content.text: Yarrow bath is a strong herbal brew of dried yarrow herb strained into a warm bath, a traditional

preparation for aching, tired, or stiff legs after prolonged standing, heavy work, or poor circulation. The warmth of the bath and the warming action of the yarrow work together to ease muscle tension and bring blood to the surface. A classic end-of-week preparation. The brew colours the bath water pale gold.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: dried yarrow herb (leaf and flower); use 25 g for a foot bath only

content.text: Place 100 g of dried yarrow in a large saucepan with 2 litres of cold water. Bring to a simmer and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Strain through a sieve, pressing the herb to extract as much liquid as possible. The herbal brew should be a golden-green colour.
Pour the herbal brew into a warm bath (or foot tub for a foot bath). The water temperature should be comfortably warm, not hot, which would increase swelling.
Soak for 20 minutes. Rest with the legs elevated afterwards.
Once or twice weekly for general fatigue and muscle aching. For acute post-exercise soreness, use on the evening of exertion.
Dried yarrow stores 12 months in a sealed tin. Prepare the herbal brew fresh for each bath.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use if you have an Asteraceae allergy. Do not use for leg pain that is accompanied by redness, significant swelling, or warmth in the calf, these signs may indicate deep vein thrombosis, which needs urgent medical attention, not herbal bathing.
